key_insight: Using a randomized Hadamard transform before scalar quantization gives provable distortion guarantees comparable to dense random rotations but at much lower cost—reducing preprocessing from Θ(d^2) to O(d log d).
problem_solved: Closes the gap between theoretically clean but slow dense random-rotation quantization and fast Hadamard-based approaches that lacked provable guarantees, enabling fast, reliable vector quantization for high-dimensional ML workloads.
method: Preprocess input vectors with a randomized Hadamard transform (random sign diagonal D followed by H) to mimic a dense random rotation in O(d log d) time.
Apply scalar quantization to the transformed coordinates (uniform or low-bit quantizers) to compress vectors.
Provide a new probabilistic analysis that handles the discrete structure of HD and proves distortion/accuracy bounds comparable to dense rotations.
impact: Delivers practical, theoretically-grounded quantization that speeds up compression pipelines (similarity search, federated learning, KV caches) while keeping predictable accuracy—reducing compute and memory cost without sacrificing guarantees.

paper_title: Provable Quantization with Randomized Hadamard Transform
paper_authors: Ying Feng, Piotr Indyk, Michael Kapralov, Dmitry Krachun, Boris Prokhorov
